name: White Oak
notes: The workhorse of the South Shore. Beautiful ray flecks when quartersawn. Patience required for drying.

name: Red Oak
notes: More porous than white oak — not suitable for outdoor use without treatment. Machines beautifully.

name: White Pine
notes: Grows everywhere on the South Shore. Soft and easy to mill. Watch for pitch pockets near knots.

name: Black Cherry
notes: Darkens beautifully with light exposure. One of the finest American hardwoods. Worth every minute of patience.

name: Hard Maple
notes: Dense and demanding on blades. Keep them sharp. Curly and bird's eye patterns add significant value.

name: Black Walnut
notes: The most valuable common North American hardwood. Rarer on the South Shore but worth seeking out.

name: Eastern Red Cedar
notes: Aromatic and naturally rot-resistant. Mills beautifully but dulls blades faster than you'd expect.

name: White Ash
notes: Mostly killed by Emerald Ash Borer on the South Shore. Mill what's standing dead — it's still usable timber.
